messages:
Lena (People Ops): quick question  we have an IC moving from US -> UK on 02/01. Their PTO accruals were prorated for US start date; manager asked if we should re-prorate for EMEA entitlements and allow carryover of 3 unused US PTO days into the new year. any guidance?

Marco (EMEA HR): cross-border moves are tricky. UK statutory rules differ. We usually map prior US days to a one-time credit but can't reduce statutory minimums. Need manager approval + employee consent + payroll check for tax/residency.

Sofia (Hiring Manager): i want to be fair and keep the 3 unused days. will get employee ok.

Tom (Payroll): FYI if we credit days after move date that could be taxable depending on where pay happens. Also limit of carryover depends on local policy. recommend we document as "one-time relocation credit" and process on first UK payroll run.

PeopleOps Bot: Policy note: Cross-border PTO transfers require: manager approval, employee written consent, payroll clearance, and an exception record. See https://redwood.example/hr/relocations. Use EXC type: RELOCATION_PTO.

Lena (People Ops): proposed steps:
1) Sofia posts one-line approval here.
2) Employee signs consent email (copy into record).
3) People Ops files EXC-2026-301 and schedules HRIS one-time +3 days on 2026-02-01 mapped to UK entitlement.
4) Payroll confirms tax handling before processing.
If all agree i'll proceed.

Sofia (Hiring Manager): approve one-time transfer of 3 unused US PTO days to UK PTO bank for Riley M. on start date 2026-02-01. I confirm i'll obtain written consent from Riley.

Marco (EMEA HR): confirmed. i'll review local entitlements and update the employee record once payroll confirms.

Tom (Payroll): i'll check tax/residency impact and reply by EOD. Please attach the consent email when ready.

Lena (People Ops): thanks all. i'll file EXC-2026-301 and wait for payroll. TL;DR: allowed as one-time relocation credit with documented consent and payroll clearance. :white_check_mark:
